Let s=sqrt(a1)>0, b=a4/2, β=a3-a4²/4+2s and γ=a2+α/2+a4s. Exact polynomial identity (α x+2H)/2=(x²+bx-s)²+βx²+γx holds for all real x. If β≥0 choose γ=0 (α0=-2a2-2a4s) for global nonnegativity. If β<0 evaluate at the positive and negative roots of x²+bx-s to obtain contradictory sign bounds for γ; necessity is for ALL α. For no cycles, d/dt [(2-2αy-α²x²)e^{αy}]=α²x²e^{αy}(αx+2H) for α≠0; finite polynomial x-zero lines cannot support a nontrivial periodic orbit. For α=0, E_dot=-x²H≤0 excludes cycles similarly. Proper W=(x²+y²)/2-yφ(x), φ′=(1+x²)^−3, satisfies Wdot≤ -xF+xφ+.5φ′F²−.5φ′y²<0 outside compact by negative x^6 dominance and fixed-x negative y². Bounded complete forward orbits and unique equilibrium hyperbolic sink (λ²+a1λ+1) plus Poincare–Bendixson imply global convergence. Exact sign-changing example (1,5,-1,0) has β=1>0, H(-1/2)=−27/16, proving energy monotonicity need not hold. Finite check.py read but not treated as quantified proof.
